what_it_does: This paper tackles a core bottleneck in machine learning and scientific computing: expensive data movement between processor and memory. Rather than moving entire datasets to the processor, the work proposes a hardware-software co-design where specialized in-memory processing (compute operations performed directly where data lives in memory) handles filter and update operations. A domain-specific language lets programmers express these patterns, which get mapped to in-memory processing hardware with modest computational capabilities.
